question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(2)=-1,\,{f}^{′}(2)=-2,\,g(2)=-5,\,{g}^{′}(2)=1
$$

If $h(x)=\frac{5f(x)+4}{g(x)+6},$ find the value of ${h}^{′}(2).$
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=5f(x)+4$ and $v=g(x)+6.$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={g}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the quotient rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{v{u}^{′}-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(g(x)+6)\cdot 5{f}^{′}(x)-(5f(x)+4)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x)+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5{f}^{′}(x)(g(x)+6)-{g}^{′}(x)(5f(x)+4)}{(g(x)+6)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =\frac{5{f}^{′}(2)(g(2)+6)-{g}^{′}(2)(5f(2)+4)}{(g(2)+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot (-2)\cdot (-5+6)-1\cdot (5\cdot (-1)+4)}{(-5+6)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-10)\cdot 1-(-1)}{{1}^{2}} \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
